title: SecOps intake - Brightforge security & hosting options
summary: Initial security posture discussion and hosting preferences. Brightforge is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment for PII-sensitive ML inference. Key asks: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML SSO integration, BYOK/KMS/HSM support, audit log retention/forwarding, RBAC scoping, and a short perf/latency benchmark before procurement decision.
topics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 evidence
Audit logs, retention, and SIEM forwarding (Splunk/Datadog)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
Short perf benchmark request and pilot timing
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Ethan from Redwood, AE, and Priya from our infra SE team is here.
[00:08] Jonas: Hey, Jonas here. We wanted this session to kind of map what gates we need to get through for PII inference — um — and what the options are.
[00:17] Priya: Great, thanks. Quick note, I'll probably jump into some infra specifics, sorry if I talk fast.
[00:22] Maya: No problem. To kick off, SOC2 and ISO — we need to know if you have up-to-date reports, and where logs go.
[00:29] Ethan: Yes. We have SOC 2 Type II and an ISO 27001 summary. We'll share the report — we'll follow up with the full attestations under an NDA. Our hosted offering is the fastest onramp, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, Private is VPC or air-gapped on-prem.
[00:45] Aamir: For our security team the big thing is keys: we require bring-your-own-key via our on-prem HSM for production. Is that supported? 
[00:53] Priya: We do BYOK for Private deployments via KMS integrations. For Hosted we support customer-managed keys in major cloud KMS providers, and we can do a customer HSM for Private via an HSM gateway. There are some network and op constraints for direct HSM-attached models, but it is a supported path.
[01:10] Jonas: When you say "some constraints" can you expand? We can't have key material leave our HSM.
[01:15] Priya: Right — so for Private/VPC we can keep key ops within the customer's network. For Hosted we rely on cloud KMS, so you'd need to be comfortable with cloud KMS semantics. We can do envelope encryption and keep model artifacts encrypted at rest. I will note that in some past transcriptions folks write K V cache as K V cash, sorry true--
[01:33] Jonas: (laughs) yeah we've seen that.
[01:36] Lena: Also need to confirm controls: SSO/SAML and SCIM user provisioning, RBAC, audit trails with immutable logs — and retention policy. We typically keep auth logs for 7 years. Is that feasible?
[01:48] Ethan: SSO via SAML, OIDC is supported, SCIM provisioning too. RBAC supports role templates and custom roles. Audit logs are available — we can stream to Splunk/Datadog/CloudWatch; retention depends on plan but we can export raw logs for long-term archival. 7 years is long but doable if you archive in your SIEM.
[02:06] Aamir: How granular are the logs? We need per-request tokens, model version, user id, redaction info — like not full prompt text, but metadata.
[02:14] Priya: We capture request metadata, model variant, timestamps, latency, error codes. By default payloads sensitive text isn't stored unless you opt in for debug. We also have prefix/KV caching metrics but we avoid storing raw prompts in long-term logs by default for privacy.
[02:30] Jonas: Okay, and about retention/deletion — can you do hard deletes and show proof?
[02:35] Ethan: Yes, we support retention policies per customer with TTLs and manual purge flows for Private. For Hosted we have data retention settings and can provide deletion receipts for compliance. There's also an export for audit.
[02:47] Maya: On compliance evidence: can you push the SOC2 report to our vendor portal, and provide a list of in-scope controls for the inference runtime?
[02:55] Ethan: Yes. Next step we'll drop SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, and a control mapping doc.
[03:00] Aamir: Performance — we need a small benchmark with our prompt set, 2k and 8k tokens, to see latency & cost. Would you run that in Dedicated or Hosted?
[03:10] Priya: For reproducible results we typically run benchmarks in Dedicated capacity or a Private sandbox — Hosted has multi-tenant variability. We can provision a short Dedicated pilot for 2 weeks or run self-hosted Private test if you prefer.
[03:22] Jonas: Our procurement window is tight — decision in ~6 weeks. We need security signoff + a cost model.
[03:29] Ethan: Understood. We'll aim to provide pilot pricing, expected per-token unit economics, and a sample rollout plan.
[03:36] Lena: About encryption standards — we require TLS 1.2+ for transit and AES-256 at rest. FIPS 140-2 compliance would be a nice-to-have.
[03:45] Priya: We enforce TLS 1.2/1.3. Storage uses AES-256. For FIPS, we can support FIPS endpoints in Private with specific HSM configurations, but hosted public endpoints may not be FIPS-certified by default.
[03:59] Aamir: Logging to SIEM — we use Splunk. We expect a consumable stream, schema mapping, and an RFC for retention. Can you share sample events?
[04:09] Ethan: We'll share sample syslog/JSON events and a Splunk ingestion recipe.
[04:14] Jonas: Any known gaps? For example, endpoint isolation for red team exercises?
[04:19] Priya: For Dedicated/Private you can isolate endpoints and VPC peering ensures no public egress. For Hosted we have tenant isolation but not air-gapped isolation. Also note that we have rolling model updates — you can pin model versions for canary and A/B tests.
[04:36] Maya: Data residency — we need EU region hosting for EU customers.
[04:40] Ethan: We have region controls and can pin to EU regions or provide Private in your DC.
[04:44] Lena: A couple legal asks: indemnity language and subprocessor list.
[04:49] Ethan: We'll provide a current subprocessor list and standard indemnity language; we can flag anything unusual for legal review.
[04:55] Jonas: One more — do you provide audit logs that show who accessed model explainability or eval results? That's important for internal audits.
[05:04] Priya: Yes we log admin console actions, who changed rollout policies, who accessed eval datasets (if stored), and can include SAML subject in admin audit trails.
[05:14] Ethan: Quick recap: we'll share SOC2 & ISO artifacts under NDA, sample audit events and Splunk mapping, BYOK options and steps for Private HSM integration, a short perf plan (Dedicated pilot recommended), and a commercial/POC estimate.
[05:29] Jonas: Sounds good. We'll send over the redacted sample logs and a short prompt set.
[05:33] Ethan: Great — we'll follow up with a preliminary statement of work and the security docs.
[05:37] Lena: Can we have the security artifacts by next Monday?
[05:40] Ethan: We'll aim for Monday (2025-03-03).
[05:43] Maya: Thanks all.
[05:45] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[05:47] [call ends]
next_steps: Ethan to upload SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary to Brightforge vendor portal (NDA as needed)
Priya to propose a short Dedicated pilot plan and perf test (2k/8k tokens)
Brightforge to share redacted sample logs and prompt set
Schedule follow-up meeting to review pilot results and legal terms
action_items: Ethan Morales - Share SOC2, ISO summary, and subprocessor list - 2025-03-03
Priya Natarajan - Prepare Dedicated pilot plan + perf test recipe and run initial smoke test - 2025-03-07
Jonas Reed (Brightforge) - Provide redacted logs, retention policy, and prompt set - 2025-03-04
